chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Abu Sa'id al-Adami, from Ya'qub ibn Yazid, from Abd Rabbih ibn Nafi', from al-Habbab ibn Musa, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The one who is born in Islam as a free person is an Arab, and the one who has a covenant and fulfills it is the servant (mawla) of the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), and the one who enters Islam willingly is a migrant (muhajir).

key_terms.حَرًّا: Free person (as opposed to a slave or servant)
key_terms.مَوْلَى: Servant or master (contextual: servant of the Messenger)
key_terms.مُهَاجِرٌ: Migrant or emigrant (referring to a convert)

ai.seo_question: What are the three categories of Muslims according to Imam al-Sadiq in this hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Ma'ani al-Akhbar*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) delineates three distinct spiritual statuses: the 'Arab' (born free in Islam), the 'Mawla' (one who fulfills their covenant with the Prophet), and the 'Muhajir' (voluntary convert). This classification reflects the socio-historical context of early Islam, distinguishing between those rooted in the community's origin, those bound by treaty or allegiance, and those who actively migrate for the sake of faith, emphasizing that spiritual rank is tied to one's relationship with the covenant and the Prophet.
